title: Reflexive 4: Each Other (plural subject)
description: Some -ся verbs describe a mutual action: people do it to each other. With a plural subject (Они обнимаются), one verb covers everyone, and no partner phrase is needed.
descriptionRussian: Некоторые глаголы на -ся описывают взаимное действие — люди делают это друг другу. При множественном подлежащем (Они обнимаются) один глагол охватывает всех, и партнёр не нужен.
intro: A second job for the same ending: instead of turning the action back on one person, it spreads it between several. They hug means each of them hugs the other, with no extra word for 'each other' anywhere in the sentence. English needs two words there and Russian needs none.
rules: Reciprocal -ся verbs mean 'do something to each other': обниматься (hug), целоваться (kiss), ссориться (quarrel), здороваться (greet).
With a plural subject, one verb covers everyone and no extra word is needed: Они обнимаются means each person hugs the other.
Present plural endings are -ются or -ятся; the -ся stays -ся after a vowel: обнимаются, целуются, ссорятся, здороваются.
Past plural uses -лись (the plural -ли ends in a vowel): обнялись, поздоровались, поссорились, целовались.
examples: Друзья обнимаются при встрече. (Friends hug each other when they meet.) Present plural, -ются.
Дети целуются с бабушкой на прощание. (The children kiss goodbye.) Present plural, -уются.
Сёстры часто ссорятся из-за игрушек. (The sisters often quarrel over toys.) Present plural, -ятся.
Соседи всегда здороваются утром. (The neighbours always greet each other in the morning.) Present plural, -аются.
Друзья обнялись и пошли домой. (The friends hugged and went home.) Past plural, -лись.
Утром все поздоровались. (In the morning everyone said hello to each other.) Past plural, -лись.

tables.title: Four 'each other' verbs with a plural subject

items.promptEnglish: Friends hug each other when they meet.
items.hint: The subject Друзья is plural (they). Which ending fits 'they'?
items.explanation: The plural subject Друзья ('they') takes the 3rd-person plural form обнимаются, and the -ся keeps the 'each other' meaning.

items.promptEnglish: The neighbours always greet each other in the morning.
items.hint: Соседи is plural. Pick the 'they' ending with -ся.
items.explanation: Соседи ('they') is a plural subject, so the verb takes the plural form здороваются.

items.promptEnglish: The sisters sometimes quarrel over toys.
items.hint: Сёстры is plural. The verb ссориться takes -ятся for 'they'.
items.explanation: Сёстры ('they') is a plural subject, so ссориться takes the plural form ссорятся.

items.promptEnglish: Masha and Lena greet each other every morning.
items.hint: 'Маша и Лена' = two people = plural. Present tense.
items.explanation: 'Маша и Лена' is a plural subject, so the present-tense form is здороваются.

items.promptEnglish: Yesterday the friends hugged and went home.
items.hint: Past tense (вчера), plural subject друзья. Use -лись.
items.explanation: Вчера signals the past, and друзья is plural, so the form is обнялись (-лись for a plural subject).

blanks: Утром все соседи _____ . (In the morning all the neighbours greet each other.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Утром все соседи здороваются: the reciprocal verb takes the plural present -ются because the neighbours greet EACH OTHER.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The friends meet up on weekends.
errorCorrection.explanation: A mutual 'meet each other' action needs the -ся verb встречаться, and the plural subject Друзья takes встречаются. Встречает has no -ся and is singular, so it loses the 'each other' meaning and does not agree with Друзья.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The sisters quickly make up after a quarrel.
errorCorrection.explanation: Сёстры ('they') is plural, so the verb takes the plural мирятся (-ятся). Мирится is singular ('he/she makes up') and does not agree with a plural subject.

hints: мы (after a vowel the ending stays -ся)

sentenceBuilding.translation: Friends hug each other when they meet.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Plural subject + the 'they' form обнимаются. Subject first.

sentenceBuilding.translation: The neighbours always greet each other in the morning.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Plural subject Соседи + здороваются. Put всегда before the verb.

sentenceBuilding.translation: The children hugged and went home.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Past plural -лись: обнялись. Then 'and went home'.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Friends hug each other when they meet.
minimalPairs.explanation: The plural subject Друзья does a mutual action, so the -ся verb обнимаются ('hug each other') is correct. Without -ся the verb loses the 'each other' meaning.
Сёстры ('they') is plural, so the verb takes the plural ссорятся (-ятся). Ссорится is the singular form ('he/she quarrels') and does not agree with a plural subject.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each -ся verb by whether the action stays on one person (to oneself) or goes between people (each other).

reviewVocab.definition: hug each other (a mutual -ся verb; with a plural subject one verb covers everyone: Они обнимаются)
quarrel, argue with each other (a mutual -ся verb; plural: Сёстры ссорятся)
greet each other, say hello (a mutual -ся verb; plural: Соседи здороваются)
